problems.title: Ratio of distant geometric terms
problems.question: A geometric progression has ratio cube-root(3). Find b₂₀₀/b₁₈₂.
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.
formulas: $b_j/b_i=q^{j-i}$ when the denominator term is nonzero.
steps: The ratio is (cube-root(3))¹⁸=3⁶=729.

problems.title: Mean of seven equally spaced observations
problems.question: Seven sorted data values each exceed the preceding by 2; median is 20. Find the mean.
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.
formulas: In an arithmetic list, opposite terms have constant sum equal to twice the middle term.
steps: The data are 14,16,18,20,22,24,26. Symmetry makes the mean equal to the middle value, 20.

problems.title: A statistic unaffected by a common translation
problems.question: Which listed statistic stays unchanged when every observation increases by 25?
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.
steps: Both extrema increase by 25, so their difference stays the same. The minimum, median, mean and any mode values all increase by 25.

problems.question: A=(5,6),B=(1,10),AM:MB=2:3. Find M.
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.

problems.title: Find a collinear vector
problems.question: A=(5,7),B=(3,1),C=(11,4),D=(0,0). Which listed connecting vector is collinear with (−4,2)?
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.
formulas: Collinear nonzero vectors are scalar multiples.
steps: AC=(6,−3)=−(3/2)(−4,2), so AC is collinear. The other listed vectors do not have this component ratio.

problems.title: Pie-chart sector from a frequency
problems.question: Of 24 students, six scored 8,eight scored 9,and the rest scored 10. Find the 10-score sector angle.
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.
steps: Ten students scored 10. Their sector angle is 360°×10/24=150°.

problems.title: One die value divides the other
problems.question: Two fair dice are rolled. Find the probability that at least one value divides the other.
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.
formulas: Use 36 ordered equally likely outcomes and inclusion–exclusion.
steps: The number of ordered pairs (u,v) with u dividing v is floor(6/1)+…+floor(6/6)=6+3+2+1+1+1=14.
Reverse divisibility gives another 14, with the six equal pairs counted twice. Thus favourable count=14+14−6=22.

problems.title: Sum only positive arithmetic terms
problems.question: An arithmetic progression has a₁=15,d=−0.5. Find the sum of its positive terms.
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.
steps: aₙ>0 gives n<31, so the positive terms are n=1,…,30, with last term 0.5.

problems.title: An internal point followed by a midpoint
problems.question: In OAB, C∈AB,AC:BC=2:1; K is midpoint of OC. OA=a,OB=b. Express OK.
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.
steps: OK=a/6+b/3. The coefficients follow the opposite endpoint weights in the 2:1 division.

problems.title: Cosine between vector combinations
problems.question: a,b are perpendicular unit vectors. Find cosine between 4a+3b and 12a−5b.
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.
steps: The dot product is 4×12+3×(−5)=33. The lengths are √(16+9)=5 and √(144+25)=13.
Thus cosθ=33/65.

problems.title: Sum of divisors of a prime power
problems.question: Find the sum of positive divisors of 37¹⁹⁹.
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.

problems.title: Polygon angles in arithmetic progression
problems.question: An n-gon has interior angles in an arithmetic progression of difference 2°, with maximum 170°. Find n.
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.
steps: The progression sum is n(171−n). Set it equal to 180(n−2), giving n²+9n−360=0.
The roots are 15 and −24. Only n=15 is a polygon size, with first angle 142°, so the data are feasible.

problems.title: An alternating infinite geometric sum
problems.question: Sum bₙ=(−1/2)ⁿ for n=1,2,… .
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.

problems.title: Angle between two positive-slope lines
problems.question: Find the cosine of the smaller angle between y=√3x and y=x/√3.
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.
formulas: The inclination angles have tangents √3 and 1/√3.
steps: The inclinations are 60° and 30°, so the angle between them is 30°. Its cosine is √3/2.

problems.title: An infinite sum compared with its first three terms
problems.question: A geometric progression with |q|<1 has total-sum:first-three-sum=8:7. Find q.
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.
steps: S/S₃=1/(1−q³)=8/7 gives 1−q³=7/8, hence q³=1/8 and q=1/2. The stated ratio excludes the all-zero progression.

problems.title: Test three set identities
problems.question: I A∪(B∩A)=(A∪B)∩A; II A∖(B∩A)=(A∖B)∩A; III A∪(B∖A)=(A∪B)∖A. Which hold for every A,B?
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.
steps: I has A on each side, so is true. II has A∖B on each side, so is true.
III has A∪B on the left but B∖A on the right. For A={1},B=∅ these are {1} and ∅, disproving the identity.

problems.title: Sum a linear function over a hundred integers
problems.question: For f(x)=(x+2)/3, calculate f(1)+…+f(100).
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.

problems.title: A line tangent to a circle
problems.question: 5x+12y+8=0 is tangent to (x−2)²+(y−5)²=R². Find R>0.
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.
formulas: Radius = distance from centre to tangent line: $|Ax_0+By_0+C|/\sqrt{A^2+B^2}$.

problems.title: Reflect across a perpendicular bisector
problems.question: A=(2,5). Find B such that y=x is the perpendicular bisector of AB.
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.
steps: B must be the reflection (5,2). The midpoint (3.5,3.5) lies on y=x, and AB has slope −1, perpendicular to slope 1.

problems.title: Sum a hundred strings of nines
problems.question: a₁=9,a₂=99,a₃=999,… . Find the first 100 terms’ sum.
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.
steps: Combining terms gives (10¹⁰¹−910)/9.

problems.title: Independent events with a certain union
problems.question: A,B are independent, A∪B is certain, and P(A)=P(B)−0.2. Find P(A).
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.
steps: At least one of p,q is 1. Since p=q−0.2<q≤1, p cannot be 1. Thus q=1 and p=0.8.

problems.title: Compare two uniform random inputs
problems.question: Independently choose x,y uniformly from [0,3]. Find P(x>y).
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.
formulas: The sample square has area 9; its diagonal divides it into equal-area halves.
steps: The diagonal x=y has probability zero. The half with x>y therefore has probability 1/2=4/8.

problems.title: A component swap gives a perpendicular vector
problems.question: m=(1,0),n=(0,1). Find the angle between a and (n·a)m−(m·a)n.
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.
formulas: If a=(u,v), the second vector is (v,−u).
steps: Their dot product is uv−uv=0. For a≠0 both lengths are positive, so the angle is 90°.
For a=0 both vectors vanish and no vector angle is defined.
problems.note: The source says a is any vector. A nonzero condition is needed for the requested angle to be defined.

problems.title: Collinearity in a square with two ratios
problems.question: M is midpoint of AD in square ABCD; N∈CD,P∈BM, CN/ND=k,BP/PM=3k, and A,P,N are collinear. Find k.
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.
steps: The slopes AP and AN are 2/(3k) and 1/(k+1). Equality gives 2(k+1)=3k, so k=2. The required points then lie on their stated segments.

problems.title: A chord through the centre is a diameter
problems.question: Find the distance between intersections of 5x+2y+9=0 and (x+1)²+(y+2)²=5.
problems.idea: Use the defining formula or identity, and check all assumptions and endpoints.
steps: The centre satisfies the line: −5−4+9=0. Hence the line cuts a diameter, whose endpoints are 2√5 apart.
